title: A Product Manager Has Almost No Authority - That's the Job
description:
A PM can't order engineers to build anything, can't draw the pixels, and can't run anyone's performance review. So what do they actually do? They own the "what" and the "why" of the product, and drive outcomes through influence instead of authority: turning vague pain into a specific, testable problem statement and a prioritized plan the rest of the team can build from. This Short breaks down what a product manager is really responsible for.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/product-manager-mastery-path/level-1/01-what-is-product-management/

#Shorts

beats.narration: A product manager has almost no direct authority. They can't make engineers build anything, can't draw the pixels, can't run anyone's review. And that's the whole job.
Product management is deciding what gets built and why, so engineering can focus on how. The PM doesn't write the code, but they're accountable for the product's outcome like no one else on the team.
So how do you drive anything with no authority? Influence. You sit in interviews and support escalations to understand the problem, then get sales, support, leadership, and legal rowing the same way.
You hold the why. You turn vague pain, like users churn a lot, into a specific, testable problem statement and a plan the team can build from. That translation is the job.
